elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 9(c)(2) warrants only that "the services will be performed in conformity with this Agreement" for thirty (30) days; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard formulation appears anywhere in Section 9 or elsewhere.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1): "the Site and any software delivered hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1) sets "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" \u2014 short of the preferred 12 months.
9(c)(2) sets "a period of thirty (30) days following performance" for services, not 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 9(c): "HDI shall, at the Company's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or services."
9(c): "... or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty in 9(a)-(c); 9(a) covers only existence, authority, enforceability and non-conflict.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty appears in the inserted 9(c) or elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(1) expressly states "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Site and any software delivered hereunder will conform in all material respects to its documentation"; the deterministic period regex reported false, but the operative text plainly states ninety (90) days, so the substance is satisfied.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 9(c)(2): "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the services will be performed in conformity with this Agreement" \u2014 meets the 30-day services floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 9(c) remedy sentence: "repair or replace the non-conforming software or services."
9(c) remedy sentence: "or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services."

reasons: Finding of deviation is correct: original Section 9 contains only mutual corporate-authority warranties (9(a)) and the Globix acknowledgment (9(b)); no performance or conformance warranty, duration or remedy exists, so the fallback failed on all four material terms.

The fallback checklist is complete in operative language: 90-day software/Site conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace plus refund of fees paid. The deterministic "period \u2265 90 days" check returning false is a mechanical artifact \u2014 the rendered clause states "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery".

Preferred level is not reached (no professional/workmanlike standard, 90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 rather than 90 days for services, no compliance-with-laws and no malicious-code warranty), which is consistent with the drafter's stated fallback target.

Minimal: a single concise new subsection 9(c) is added; existing 9(a) and 9(b) are untouched, no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra damages categories, notice procedures or disclaimer carve-out is added (none needed \u2014 the agreement contains no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer).

Note (not a defect): the remedy is exercisable "at the Company's election" rather than the model language's "at Vendor's option". This is a customer-favourable parameter within the remedy element rather than an added requirement, but the drafter should expect pushback and can concede vendor election without losing the fallback.

Preserves intent: no cross-references are broken and no retained sentence is contradicted; "documentation" and "the services" are used consistently with Sections 1 and 5. If the counterparty resists, tighten "its documentation" to "the applicable documentation for the Site and such software" to remove the singular-pronoun ambiguity \u2014 a drafting polish, not a checklist gap.
